title: Lane Ownership Is For Speed, Not Territory — Do, Record, Hand Off

source.source_reference: Shawn directive via Naya5 master directive + Naya4 proposal, #1354, 2026-10-08

intelligence.essence: Lane ownership exists for speed, not territory. If a lane is active and parallel, stay in your lane. If a lane is stalled and blocking, do the thing yourself at the same quality bar, record that you did it, notify the owner, and hand them their next task. Waiting because "it's their job" is the bottleneck.

human_view.subject: Don't wait — do, record, hand off
human_view.text: Assign lane work to parallelize, never to create fiefdoms. If a lane is active and parallel, stay in your lane. If someone is stalled and blocking — for any reason — do the thing yourself: same quality bar, record that you did it, notify the owner, hand them their next task. Waiting because "it's their job" is the bottleneck.

intelligence.simple_view: Don't wait on someone else's lane. If they are stuck and blocking you, do it yourself, write down what you did, tell them, and give them their next task.

naya_view.text: Operating rule for all seats: active+parallel -> stay in lane; stalled+blocking -> take and go. Always leave a receipt: what done, where recorded, next owner.

learning_lesson.text: Authority-by-seat must not become permission-to-stall. Escalate past bottlenecks by executing, not waiting.
